intro_notes: NOTE: Choose THREE groups that have different racial, cultural, national, or ethnic backgrounds, one of which comes from your own background. Use these groups to meet requirements 1, 2, and 3.
NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.lead_text: Do TWO of the following, choosing a different group for each:
requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following, choosing a different group for each: (a) Go to a festival, celebration, or other event identified with one of the groups. Report on what you see and learn. (b) Go to a place of worship, school, or other institution identified with one of the groups. Report on what you see and learn. (c) Talk with a person from one of the groups about the heritage and traditions of the group. Report on what you learn. (d) Learn a song, dance, poem, or story that is traditional to one group, and teach it to a group of your friends. (e) Go to a library or museum to see a program or exhibit featuring one group's traditions. Report on what you see and learn.

pamphlet_excerpts: Imagine that one of the groups: What if one of the groups you are exploring had always livedalone in a city or country, with no contact with any othergroups (p. 46).
Imagine that one of the groups Principle 2: What do you think the city or country would be liketoday (p. 46).
Imagine that one of the groups Principle 3: What would it be like if all three of your groups livedthere at the same time (p. 46).
Imagine that one of the groups Principle 4: For requirement 2, you must stretch your imagination (p. 46).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Imagine that one of the groups): Picture yourself in a different cultural group and imagine whatyour life would be like in that society if it had always beenisolated (p. 46).
Step 2 (Imagine that one of the groups): In this situation, members of the community would have no technology borrowed from other groups, and no idea that other cultures exist (p. 46).
Step 3 (Imagine that one of the groups): Do you think the group would be hunting with spears, sheltering in caves, and wearing clothes made of leaves andtree bark (p. 46).
Step 4 (Imagine that one of the groups): Would it be a modern society with planes, television, and video games (p. 46).

pamphlet_excerpts: About Some Differences: Old family photographs offer glimpses of the past and mayprovide significant clues about your own cultural background (p. 40).
About Some Differences Principle 2: Many Americans can trace their origins back to severalcountries (p. 40).

About Some Differences Principle 3: It's common for an American to have a multiculturalheritage, that is, to keep family traditions or customs that have been passed down from several cultures (p. 40).
About Some Differences Principle 4: Some families know agreat deal about their history and preserve their heritage in dailylife (p. 40).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (About Some Differences): Other families know very little about their backgrounds (p. 40).
Step 2 (About Some Differences): Your family may enjoy learning with you as you explore theculture of your ancestors (p. 40).
Step 3 (About Some Differences): It is not necessary to research your family's backgroundbefore you talk with them, but it is very important to do sobefore you talk (p. 40).
Step 4 (About Some Differences): When you think you have found enough information inbooks and (with permission) on the internet, you are ready for the next step: preparing (p. 40).
